sections.title: The partnership, before the product.
cols: Your machine leaves the factory with a panel HMI and nothing behind it: no record the plant keeps, no history, no maintenance system, and a service contract that begins when something breaks. With SOP on board it leaves with its own pages, its record, its maintenance package, and a desk you open from your office.
No server at the client, nothing licensed per screen — and every service line yours.
Your machines, and your client — you put SOP on every machine and line you build, in every country you sell to. You own the end client, and that is written into the agreement.

No server to install at the client — the machine's edge talks to a server on the cloud backbone, provisioned for that client plant and kept by us. You point it, then develop, commission and maintain the line from your office.

Your service knowledge, on board — your engineers author the machine's type package once: parts with your own numbers, plans, checklists, failure causes. It plants itself in every plant the machine lands in, and the standard project travels as one file.
Every service line yours — commissioning, the type package, remote assistance, optimisation visits and the on-premises server option are entirely your revenue.
What you ship is not a nicer panel — it is the complete execution system and the complete maintenance system, on the SCADA's own database, on the controller your machine already carries.

cols: The machine writes its own history from the day it is commissioned, and the plant keeps it. In the control room that history is an instrument the operator finishes; from your office it is the night you were not there, played back on the operator's own screen.

sections.title: The second lens: over the tags.
cols: Two lenses: one over time, one over the tags — each answers from the one database.
The transport bar — the alarms active at that moment, commands off, the day's timeline, the speeds, go to a moment, back to live.
From an alarm row, one press shows the page as it was when the alarm fired.

Change a delivered signal — renamed, re-addressed or dropped: the what-if painter shows every page, trend, alarm and report block that would feel it, each with its own fate, before you touch anything.
The health sweep, before the machine ships — signals polled and shown nowhere, bindings pointing at nothing, formulas that no longer parse; reports and conditions are in the thread too.
Why a machine builder cares — a machine already delivered is still yours to change: the Tag Lens shows what a signal touches before you move it, on a line that is not in your building.
We know of no other platform that follows one tag through every module of the plant like this.

sections.title: No server at the client: the remote desk
No server at the client. Every machine on your desk.
cols: Every client plant gets a server of its own, provisioned by us on the cloud backbone from scripts, in a single session. You point the machine's edge at it, and from that day you develop the line, commission it and maintain it from your own office.
A server per client plant — one client, one server, never two clients sharing one.

The edge holds the line — it sits beside the controller and never asks the backbone for permission to work: cut the link and it holds the readings on its own disk and sends them on when the link returns.
The pages on the plant network — while the backbone is unreachable the edge serves the machine's real pages on the plant network, behind a password the administrator armed once.
The armed emergency access — armed once by the administrator, and refused while the backbone is healthy.
The desk, by the plant's grant — a scope on the machine's edge or on its line, nothing wider: live pages, journal, trend, replay, and a fix drawn in the browser and saved to the project.
The plant can withdraw the grant, which is why it gives it.
The client's own server, your option — a client who wants its line on its own hardware gets it, installed and maintained by you, at your price; everything else on the page is identical.
The fleet page — every machine you delivered, the line it runs and when it last spoke.
Not one of these changes a screen anybody uses: you point the edge at an address, and everything after it is a grant the plant gives and can take back.

sections.title: The line runs its orders. The machine runs its own maintenance.
cols: Your machine already knows what it made and what stopped it. The execution system and the maintenance system are not two more products to buy and join: they are the same database as the pages the operator watches, and they leave your factory with the machine. Your client gets one line, one contract, one screen. You get a service business that begins on the day of delivery.

The order is on the line, not on a clipboard beside it. A job opens and closes on the machine's own signals — a vessel charge or a packer count — and the batches inside it open and close the same way; they overlap.
The batch record says how — line by line, how every number is known: counted, weighed, or left as the balance that does not close; the handover and the certificate print from the same rows.
The machine knows its own service — a stop or an alarm becomes a job from the alarm itself, with the reason already on it.
The job on a phone — why it is due now, the parts and whether the shelf has them, the window the line has protected, the checklist to tick, measure and photograph.
Your part numbers on the close — nothing is keyed twice and nothing is filed later; the close seals a record your service desk reads, and the parts carry your part numbers.
Integrated by birth — what was made, what stopped it and what was repaired print from the same rows the operator watched. Nothing to connect, because there is nothing to connect.
The laboratory outranks the counter — a reject signed by the laboratory outranks the counter, and the period says it was restated.

sections.title: From the machine to the signed sheet.
cols: The paper is the part of the machine your client keeps. Here the machine writes it: the acceptance that proves the rate you promised, the certificate that follows every batch, the review of what your service did all month. Designed once against the machine's own tags, computed on the server, sealed, signed by name and delivered, with nobody watching.
01 Design — blocks bound to the machine's own tags: tiles against the rate you promised, period tables, trends with limits, the alarm journal, the loss cascade, maintenance blocks.
02 Compute — on the server, in the plant's own clock: every shift, day, week or month, every batch or order, every maintenance job, or when a plant condition fires.
03 Seal — frozen on arrival, numbered, fingerprinted; run it again and a second document is filed beside the first, never a refresh of it.
04 Sign — by name and capacity, proved with the signer's own password, bound to the fingerprint, never edited and never withdrawn; an acceptance carries both sides.
05 Deliver — printed on the client's letterhead in three languages, sent to the list, filed as a document, exported.

Judged against the promised rate — over the window the contract names, every hour that did not become product is on the sheet and timed: not asked to run, breakdowns, small stops with the operator's reason, speed loss, rejects.
The same sheet proves the gain — nothing is left to argue about, and the same sheet proves the gain when you come back to make the line quicker.
Zero report servers — the engine runs on the backend the machine already talks to; a small worker beside it files the document and sends it on.
Zero third-party licences — no reporting product, no rendering licence, no designer bought separately: it is an organ of the platform.
Zero seats to read — every operator, supervisor, planner and auditor at the client reads, prints, exports and signs.

sections.title: The partnership, item by item.
rows: The backbone, no site visit

A server for each client plant, provisioned by us on the cloud backbone from scripts, in a single session. You install nothing at the client, unless the client wants a server of its own: your priced option.
The line runs without the link

SOP supports all major drivers — Modbus, OPC DA, Siemens S7 and OPC UA among them — to the controllers you already ship. Where a machine family needs a driver or a function of its own, we build it: the work of the alliance.
Your project travels as one file

The standard project exports by name, with its symbols, faceplates, trends, alarms, documents and equipment types inside, and imports on any server without a collision. One machine, one file, every plant.
Annual training and support

Your service engineers trained every year on the platform and every module, with the manuals, the flight-test documents and the demonstration plant; unlimited technical support behind every machine you ship.
Powered by SOP, in your brand

Your symbols and pages, your letterhead on every printed record, your part numbers on the type package, your name on the service. The platform keeps its mark on the applications, and the clause is in every agreement.
